zurngtest

Overview

A random number generator can pass every statistical test you know of and still fail the one that matters for your simulation. The test suite that the current literature on generator design reports against is PractRand, by Chris Doty-Humphrey: it tests a stream of bits at doubling lengths and reports the length at which a generator first fails. Until now, using it from R meant writing bytes to a file and running its command-line tool.

zurngtest runs PractRand from R:

  • PractRand’s own verdicts. The core and expanded batteries of PractRand 0.96, with its labels and thresholds unchanged. With the core battery, pract_test() gives the results PractRand’s own RNG_test gives for the same bytes, which a continuous-integration job checks.
  • R’s generators on their own bits. pract_rng() recovers the integers behind runif() for each RNGkind() where they exist, and leaves the session’s random numbers as they were.
  • Any source of bits. Raw bytes, connections, R functions, and combinations of them, such as two seeds of one generator interleaved.
  • A fast path for generator packages. Generators written in C hand their words to PractRand directly, at about the speed of RNG_test.
  • No dependencies beyond R. PractRand is bundled, and zurngtest imports only base R’s stats.

Installation

zurngtest is not on CRAN yet. Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zurngtest")

Usage 

library(zurngtest)

The low byte of a linear congruential generator repeats every 256 values. PractRand needs a few kilobytes to see it:

lcg_low_bits <- local({
  x <- 1
  function(n) {
    out <- raw(n)
    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      x <<- (1664525 * x + 1013904223) %% 2^32
      out[i] <- as.raw(x %% 256)
    }
    out
  }
})
pract_test(pract_fun(lcg_low_bits, bits = 8), min_bytes = 2^12, max_bytes = 2^14)
#> PractRand 0.96 test of function lcg_low_bits, 8-bit words
#> length= 4 kilobytes (2^12 bytes)
#>   Test Name                         p-value       Evaluation
#>   BCFN(2+0,13-9U)                   1.00e-28      FAIL !!!
#>   DC6-9x1Bytes-1                    2.66e-56      FAIL !!!!
#>   Gap-16:A                          0.00e+00      FAIL !!!!!!!!
#>   Gap-16:B                          0.00e+00      FAIL !!!!!!!!
#>   Gap-16:C                          1.00e+00      mildly suspicious
#>   FPF/16:all                        0.00e+00      FAIL !!!!!!!
#>   FPF/16:cross                      0.00e+00      FAIL !!!!!!!
#>   mod3n(5):(2,9-6)                  5.23e-06      suspicious
#>   ...and 4 test result(s) without anomalies
#> Failed at 4 kilobytes (2^12 bytes), time= 0.3 seconds

R’s default generator, Mersenne-Twister, tested on its own 32-bit integers, does not fail over the first 4 megabytes. An “unusual” result now and then is what a good generator gives; a “FAIL” is not:

pract_test(pract_rng("Mersenne-Twister", seed = 1), min_bytes = 2^20, max_bytes = 2^22)
#> PractRand 0.96 test of R's Mersenne-Twister generator (seed 1), its 32-bit integers
#> length= 1 megabyte (2^20 bytes)
#>   no anomalies in 80 test result(s)
#> length= 2 megabytes (2^21 bytes)
#>   no anomalies in 90 test result(s)
#> length= 4 megabytes (2^22 bytes)
#>   Test Name                         p-value       Evaluation
#>   [Low1/32]DC6-9x1Bytes-1           0.00141       unusual
#>   ...and 98 test result(s) without anomalies
#> No failure, time= 1.2 seconds

Seeding schemes deserve testing too, since a combination of streams can fail where each stream passes. Two seeds of Mersenne-Twister, interleaved word by word, pass:

seeds <- pract_interleave(pract_rng(seed = 1), pract_rng(seed = 2))
res <- pract_test(seeds, min_bytes = 2^20, max_bytes = 2^21)

The result is a data frame with one row per test and length, and the first failing length, if any, in its failed_at attribute:

attr(res, "failed_at")
#> [1] NA
head(as.data.frame(res), 3)
#>     bytes            test   p_value evaluation
#> 1 1048576 BCFN(2+0,13-7U) 0.7821732     normal
#> 2 1048576 BCFN(2+1,13-7U) 0.9186383     normal
#> 3 1048576 BCFN(2+2,13-8U) 0.6471684     normal

Related work

PractRand is by Chris Doty-Humphrey and is in the public domain; zurngtest bundles version 0.96 with a few patches, described in the package’s src/practrand/PROVENANCE. On CRAN, RDieHarder runs the older DieHarder suite.
